subject: Advance-commitment packaging for NimbusHealth — approval needed
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Laura Andrews <laura.andrews@nimbushealth.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Advance-commitment packaging for NimbusHealth — approval needed

Hi Laura / Nimbus procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As discussed, attached is the SOW v3 and a workbook that lays out two packaging options:

- Option A (Onramp + Dedicated): 18-month advance commitment for 4 dedicated units, prefunded with monthly drawdown.
- Option B (Burst-first): 12-month advance commitment + burst capacity blocks that scale during onboarding spikes.

Key ask: Nimbus has requested a one-time onboarding credit and a softer ramp rate for months 1–3 to align with their clinical integration timeline. Specifically they are asking for a $200k onboarding credit and an effective blended rate ~22% below our standard entry slab for the first year.

Proposed next step from my side is to escalate for internal approval for a structured concession (onboarding credit + conditional discount floor) and to lock the legal guardrails (true-up, termination with cure, data residency clause). Can you confirm what additional detail you need for approval?

Attachments: NimbusHealth_SOW_v3.pdf, redwood-pricing-model-nimbus.xlsx

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
(415) 555-0124

From: Laura Andrews <laura.andrews@nimbushealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com, Peter Shaw <peter.shaw@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Advance-commitment packaging for NimbusHealth — approval needed

Jordan,

Thanks for the materials — doc looks clean. A few follow-ups from our side before we move to legal:

1) The onboarding timeline is front-loaded: months 1–3 will see 60–80% of token consumption. We need a soft ramp (lower effective rate) to avoid early budget strain.
2) The dedicated pool in Option A is attractive, but can you confirm VPC connectivity timelines and whether dedicated instances can be burstable for the first 90 days?
3) We can accept a true-up but require the true-up to be annual (not quarterly) and ask that the onboarding credit be applied as a prepayment offset, not a separate rebate.

Procurement asked if Redwood can consider a $200k onboarding credit against the first-year invoice and a 15–22% effective discount on year-one consumption compared to list. Our procurement window closes 09/30 — we need terms by next week.

Best,
Laura Andrews
Head of Integrations\NimbusHealth
laura.andrews@nimbushealth.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Advance-commitment packaging for NimbusHealth — summarize & ask for approval

Marissa / Kim — forwarding Nimbus response and procurement ask. Short summary + recommendation below.

Summary:
- Account: NimbusHealth (Strategic prospect; expected 3–4x expansion after EHR integration).
- Request: $200k onboarding credit applied to year-1 invoice + effective 15–22% discount Y1; annual true-up preferred; VPC/dedicated ramp/burst capability for first 90 days.
- Timing: Procurement expects terms by 2026-09-30.

Commercial impact if approved:
- Initial FY1 revenue (net of credit): ~$450k–$550k depending on consumption pattern.
- Gross margin hit from credit + discount: estimated 18–25% on year-1 unit economics.
- Upside: projected multi-year ARR if integration goes smooth (~$2M ARR by year 2).

Recommendation (two-track):
A) Approve a conditional onboarding credit of $200k applied as prepayment offset plus a 15% guaranteed floor discount for months 1–12; include an annual true-up instead of quarterly true-up.
B) Require a 12-month initial commit (instead of 18) with an option to extend to 24 if usage thresholds met; hold the bulk of concession in the first-year accounting (i.e., the credit applied to year-1 invoice) and require DocuSign & procurement acceptance.

If we pursue A + B we keep downside limited (12-month legal guardrails) while giving Nimbus the near-term rate relief they need. Requesting formal approval from Finance (Markus) and a legal redline path.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-model-nimbus.xlsx

Can you advise whether we have flexibility on the annual true-up ask and whether Finance can accept the margin hit for year-1 on the grounds of strategic expansion? I can sketch a concise approval memo for exec sign-off.

—Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal memo: Recommended concession for NimbusHealth (ND-2026-042) — request VP Finance sign-off

Markus —

Quick memo and recommendation for your review. We need VP/Finance sign-off to meet Nimbus procurement timeline (they need commercial terms by 09/30). Below are facts, impact, and recommended controls.

Deal snapshot:
- Account: NimbusHealth (prospect -> strategic customer, clinical integrations planned Q1 2027)
- Proposed structure: 12-month advance-commitment, onboarding credit applied to Year-1 invoice, 15% guaranteed discount floor for months 1–12, annual true-up.
- Attachments: internal-approval-memo.pdf (detailed P&L impact), pricing workbook.

Financial impact (concise):
- Upfront onboarding credit: $200,000 (applied against invoice)
- Expected net FY1 revenue: $480,000 (model median scenario)
- Estimated FY1 gross margin after concession: ~62% (vs. standard ~80%) — margin impact primarily in year-1.

Strategic rationale:
- High pipeline conversion probability with EHR vendor already committed to pilot.
- Significant cross-sell possibilities in care management modules; conservative estimate +$1.6M ARR in 24 months.

Recommended guardrails if approved:
1) Limit concession to a single-account SOW and attach a strict true-up clause at 12 months.
2) Include a termination-for-convenience close-out that requires procurement to pay consumed capacity through termination date.
3) Require procurement to execute redlined SOW via DocuSign within 10 business days of receiving final doc; credit is void if executed later than 30 days after offer date.
4) Include a 12-month minimum commit with a usage threshold clause to trigger the 24-month extension and any deeper discounts.

Ask: Markus, please confirm approval (or alternate guidance). If approved, Jordan will notify the customer and legal will prepare the SOW/DocuSign flow.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Sales Operations
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal memo: Recommended concession for NimbusHealth (ND-2026-042) — request VP Finance sign-off

Marissa / team —

Reviewed the memo and model. Approve the concession with the following mandatory conditions:

1) Credit structure: $200k applied strictly as a prepayment offset on the first invoice (not a rebate).
2) Term: 12-month minimum commit; extension to 24 months only if the usage threshold of 120% of committed units is hit in months 10–12.
3) True-up: annual true-up retained; any material underrun (<60% of committed consumption) triggers clawback of a prorated portion of the onboarding credit.
4) DocuSign + procurement: legal to circulate redlined SOW within 48 hours of this approval; deal must be signed within 10 business days to preserve credit.

I accept the FY1 margin impact under the rationale that this is a strategic account with high conversion probability. Please ensure the SOW includes the termination protections and that CS is looped for onboarding support SLA.

Approval: MARKUS KLEIN, VP Finance — APPROVED 2026-09-19 09:37 PDT

Please proceed.
Markus

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Laura Andrews <laura.andrews@nimbushealth.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Advance-commitment packaging for NimbusHealth — approval needed

Laura / Nimbus procurement —

Good news: Finance has approved the onboarding credit and the conditional discount structure. High level summary of approved terms follows (detailed SOW will be sent via DocuSign shortly):

- Onboarding credit: $200,000 applied as prepayment offset on the first invoice.
- Commit: 12-month minimum advance-commitment (Option B variant).
- Discount: 15% guaranteed effective floor for months 1–12 (applied to committed units).
- True-up: Annual true-up; material underrun (<60%) triggers a prorated clawback of the onboarding credit.
- Extension: Option to extend to 24 months if usage >=120% of committed units in months 10–12.
- Timing: Legal will send updated SOW via DocuSign; signature required within 10 business days to preserve credit. DocuSign link will be sent from legal (tracking: https://www.docusign.net/execute?docId=abc123).

We appreciate the urgency; if this aligns with your procurement needs I’ll ask Legal to publish the redlined SOW immediately. Once signed we will kick off onboarding and allocate a dedicated onboarding manager for the first 90 days.

Next steps: Please confirm you want us to proceed on the above and we’ll route the DocuSign flow.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
